lines.trans: Good morning! It smells like warm cinnamon all the way up on the stairs!

words.gloss: to smell (oler a = to smell of/like)

lines.trans: Good morning, Madam Carmen! My cinnamon rolls just came out of the oven.
Sit down by the sunny window, madam! No rush to go upstairs yet!
Actually, I only came down to ask why the bathroom tap ran so chilly.
Chilly? Ah, yes! Our neighbourhood pipes stretch slowly in the morning!
Have a hot cup of tea and a cinnamon roll for ten minutes first!
Well, nobody sensible says no to warm cinnamon bread at seven in the morning.
Wonderful choice! Would you like honey or apple jam on the side?
Just a little butter, thank you. Why do you keep looking at your watch, sir?
Me? Oh, I simply adore punctuality! Seven fourteen is a lovely minute!

words.gloss: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)

lines.trans: Look through the courtyard window, Ernesto: someone just ran in!
Saved! Excuse me one moment, madam, enjoy your hot tea!
See you!

meanings.note: Shortens to buen before masculine singular nouns (buen viaje); ¡Buenos días! = Good morning!

examples.trans: Good morning, everyone!
The weather is very nice today.

meanings.note: Masculine despite ending in -a: el día, ¡Buenos días!.

examples.trans: The day is here.

examples.text: Vemos los días desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the days from the door.

oler.gloss: to smell (oler a = to smell of/like)

meanings.en: to smell (oler a = to smell of/like)
meanings.note: Irregular boot stem hue- (huelo, hueles, huele, huelen).

examples.text: La cocina huele a canela caliente.
examples.trans: The kitchen smells like warm cinnamon.

examples.text: El jardín huele a flores frescas.
examples.trans: The garden smells of fresh flowers.

meanings.note: Marks destination, clock time, and animate direct objects (personal a).

examples.trans: We are going to the station now.

examples.text: El desayuno empieza a las ocho.
examples.trans: Breakfast starts at eight o'clock.

meanings.note: Fragrant baking spice.

examples.text: La canela es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The cinnamon is very important here.
We talk about the cinnamon.

meanings.note: Describes hot drinks, food, or water.

examples.trans: It is a hot piece.

examples.text: Aquí tiene, señora: té caliente de menta con miel.
examples.trans: Here you are, madam: hot mint tea with honey.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta luego! = See you later!; ¡Hasta mañana! = See you tomorrow!

examples.trans: Walk straight ahead as far as the bridge.
We are staying until Friday.

meanings.note: Opposite of abajo.

examples.trans: The bedrooms are upstairs.
Look up toward the balcony.

meanings.note: Expresses location inside or on top of a surface (en la mesa = on the table).

examples.text: Las tazas están en la mesa.
examples.trans: The cups are on the table.

examples.text: Vivimos en Valencia todo el año.
examples.trans: We live in Valencia all year.

meanings.note: Definite feminine singular article before nouns; direct-object feminine pronoun before/attached to verbs.

examples.text: La puerta del patio es azul.
examples.trans: The courtyard door is blue.
The room has plenty of light.

meanings.note: Often singular (la escalera) or plural (las escaleras) for a staircase.

examples.trans: The stairs is here.

examples.text: Vemos las escaleras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the stairss from the door.

meanings.note: Polite form of address: señora Carmen.

examples.trans: The madam is here.

examples.text: Vemos las señoras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the madams from the door.

meanings.note: Plural mis (mi llave / mis llaves); unaccented, distinct from pronoun mí.

examples.trans: My suitcase is navy blue.

examples.text: Mis apuntes están en el bolsillo.
examples.trans: My notes are in my pocket.

meanings.note: Baked pastry roll or scroll.

examples.trans: The roll is here.

examples.text: Vemos los rollos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the rolls from the door.

meanings.note: Links possession, origin, material (de madera), and contents (taza de té).

examples.text: Es una mesa redonda de madera.
examples.trans: It is a round wooden table.

examples.text: Vengo de la estación de tren.
examples.trans: I am coming from the train station.

acabar.gloss: to finish; to have just (acabar de)

meanings.en: to finish; to have just (acabar de)
meanings.note: Acabar de + infinitive means 'to have just done something'.

examples.trans: I have just arrived from the market.

examples.text: Ya acabamos el trabajo de hoy.
examples.trans: We already finished today's work.

salir.gloss: to go out; to come out; to leave

meanings.en: to go out; to come out; to leave
meanings.note: Irregular 1st sg salgo; salir corriendo = run out.

examples.text: El pan acaba de salir del horno.
examples.trans: The bread just came out of the oven.
I leave early for the station.

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition de + masculine article el.

examples.text: El bizcocho acaba de salir del horno.
examples.trans: The cake just came out of the oven.
I am a neighbour from the quarter.

meanings.note: Del horno = out of the oven.

examples.trans: The oven is here.

examples.text: Vemos los hornos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the ovens from the door.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (e -> ie: me siento, ¡siéntese!).

examples.text: Siéntese junto a la ventana, por favor.
examples.trans: Sit down by the window, please.
We sit down under the lemon tree.

meanings.note: Junto a + noun works like a preposition meaning 'beside / next to'.

examples.trans: Sit next to the window.
We work together at the guesthouse.

meanings.note: Una ventana soleada = a sunny window.

examples.trans: The window is here.

examples.text: Vemos las ventanas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the windows from the door.

meanings.note: Una ventana soleada = a sunny window.

examples.trans: It is a sunny piece.
The old sunny attic room... follow me, quickly!

meanings.note: Placed directly before the verb (or object pronouns) to negate a sentence.

examples.trans: Today it is not raining in Valencia.

examples.text: No se preocupe por la hora.
examples.trans: Do not worry about the time.

tener.gloss: to have; to have to (tener que + inf)

meanings.en: to have; to have to (tener que + inf)
meanings.note: Used in idioms: tener hambre/frío/miedo/prisa/razón; tener que = must.

examples.trans: We have eight quiet rooms.

examples.text: Tengo que cerrar la ventana ahora.
examples.trans: I have to close the window now.

meanings.note: Tener prisa = be in a rush; ¡Date prisa! = Hurry up!

examples.trans: The hurry is here.

examples.text: Vemos las prisas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the hurrys from the door.

por.gloss: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)

meanings.en: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)
meanings.note: Por la mañana = in the morning; por favor = please; gracias por = thanks for.

examples.trans: We stroll through the old quarter.

examples.text: Por la mañana entra mucho sol.
examples.trans: In the morning plenty of sun comes in.

subir.gloss: to go up; to climb; to carry upstairs

meanings.en: to go up; to climb; to carry upstairs
meanings.note: Works both intransitively and transitively.

examples.text: Subo las toallas limpias a la primera planta.
examples.trans: I carry the clean towels up to the first floor.

examples.text: Subieron despacio la escalera de madera.
examples.trans: They climbed the wooden stairs slowly.

meanings.note: Everyday word for 'still' or 'not yet'.

examples.trans: The coffee is still hot.
It is not twelve o'clock yet.

meanings.note: En realidad softens a correction ('actually / in fact').

examples.text: La realidad es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The reality is very important here.
We talk about the reality.

solo.gloss: only; just (also adj solo/sola = alone / single)

meanings.en: only; just (also adj solo/sola = alone / single)
meanings.note: Unaccented in modern RAE spelling; café solo = black espresso.

examples.trans: I only need five more minutes.
Only a single room remains vacant.

bajar.gloss: to go down; to bring down; to lower

meanings.en: to go down; to bring down; to lower
meanings.note: Works both intransitively (go downstairs) and transitively (bring down).

examples.text: Bajo a la cocina a preparar té.
examples.trans: I go down to the kitchen to make tea.

examples.text: Bajamos las maletas por la escalera.
examples.trans: We bring the suitcases down the stairs.

meanings.note: Preguntar asks a question; pedir asks for an item or favour.

examples.text: Pregunto en la farmacia por la calle.
examples.trans: I ask at the pharmacy about the street.

examples.text: Una clienta preguntó por el desayuno.
examples.trans: A guest asked about breakfast.

qué.gloss: what?; which?; how / what a! (in exclamations)

meanings.en: what?; which?; how / what a! (in exclamations)
meanings.note: Used in questions (¿qué hora es?) and exclamations (¡qué alivio!).

examples.trans: What time is it right now?
What a bright morning!

meanings.note: Definite article; also appears before feminine nouns starting with stressed /a/ (el agua, el asa).

examples.trans: The courtyard has plenty of light.
Pass me the reservation book.

meanings.note: Water tap in a sink or shower.

examples.trans: The tap is here.

examples.text: Vemos los grifos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the taps from the door.

meanings.note: Cuarto de baño or simply el baño.

examples.trans: The bathroom is here.

examples.text: Vemos los baños desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the bathrooms from the door.

meanings.note: Shortened form of tanto used before adjectives and adverbs (¡qué mañana tan luminosa!).

examples.trans: What a peaceful courtyard!

examples.text: ¿Por qué sale el agua tan fría?
examples.trans: Why is the water running so cold?

meanings.note: As a masculine noun (el frío), means 'the cold'.

examples.trans: It is a cold piece.

examples.text: Aquí tiene un paño limpio y agua fría, Ernesto.
examples.trans: Here is a clean cloth and cold water, Ernesto.

meanings.note: Expresses sudden realization or understanding.

examples.trans: Ah, now I understand the map!
Oh really? What good news.

meanings.note: Accented sí means 'yes' (distinct from unaccented si = 'if').

examples.trans: Yes, the room is ready.
Of course, come right in!

meanings.note: Used with feminine plural nouns and clock hours (las ocho).

examples.trans: The windows face the garden.
We have breakfast at eight.

meanings.note: Water or heating pipe.

examples.trans: The pipe is here.

examples.text: Vemos las tuberías desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the pipes from the door.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender and number with the thing possessed (nuestro patio, nuestra posada).

examples.trans: Our guesthouse has eight rooms.
Our neighbours have coffee here.

meanings.note: Local city district with its own shops and squares.

examples.trans: The neighbourhood is here.

examples.text: Vemos los barrios desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the neighbourhoods from the door.

se.gloss: himself / herself / yourself / themselves; impersonal one

meanings.en: himself / herself / yourself / themselves; impersonal one
meanings.note: Reflexive, reciprocal, passive/impersonal pronoun, and indirect object le/les before lo/la.

examples.trans: The door opens slowly.

examples.text: Aquí se oye el canto de los pájaros.
examples.trans: Here you can hear the birds singing.

meanings.note: Built from shaking off pereza (sleepy laziness).

examples.text: Me desperezo al abrir la ventana.
examples.trans: I stretch awake when opening the window.

examples.text: El barrio se despereza poco a poco.
examples.trans: The neighbourhood stretches awake little by little.

meanings.note: Everyday single-word opposite of rápido.

examples.trans: Walk slowly on the stairs.
Turn the wheel very slowly.

meanings.note: La mañana = the morning; mañana (without article) = tomorrow.

examples.text: Por la mañana servimos café caliente.
examples.trans: In the morning we serve hot coffee.
See you tomorrow at eight!

meanings.note: ¡Toma! = Here you go!; tomar un café = have a coffee.

examples.trans: What would you like to have for breakfast?
Here you go, here is the flashlight.

meanings.note: Shortens to primer before masculine singular nouns (el primer día); also used as adverb ('first').

examples.text: Hoy es mi primer día de trabajo.
examples.trans: Today is my first day of work.
The first room is vacant.

meanings.note: Forms: un (m sg), una (f sg), unos (m pl 'some/about'), unas (f pl).

examples.text: Quiero un café caliente, por favor.
examples.trans: I would like a hot coffee, please.

examples.text: Hay una mesa libre en el patio.
examples.trans: There is a free table in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Una taza de té = a cup of tea.

examples.trans: The cup is here.

examples.text: Vemos las tazas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the cups from the door.

meanings.note: Accented té ('tea') distinguishes the noun from pronoun te ('you').

examples.trans: The tea is here.

examples.text: Vemos los tés desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the teas from the door.

meanings.note: Changes to e before words starting with /i/ sound (i- or hi-).

examples.text: Servimos café caliente y pan fresco.
examples.trans: We serve hot coffee and fresh bread.
It is quarter past seven.

meanings.note: Diez sobre diez = ten out of ten.

examples.trans: There are ten minutes left before starting.
Your front desk deserves a ten.

meanings.note: En cinco minutos = in five minutes.

examples.trans: The minute is here.

examples.text: Vemos los minutos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the minutes from the door.

meanings.note: Requires no before the verb when nadie follows (no hay nadie).

examples.text: Todavía no hay nadie en el patio.
examples.trans: There is nobody in the courtyard yet.
Nobody knows this building better.

meanings.note: False friend: means 'sensible', whereas 'sensitive' is sensible!

examples.trans: It is a sensible piece.
sensible

meanings.note: Querer decir means 'to mean'.

examples.trans: What does the letter say exactly?
Tell me the truth without fear.

meanings.note: Core connector and relative pronoun (unaccented, distinct from interrogative qué).

examples.trans: I hope that you rest very well.

examples.text: El pan de esta panadería huele genial.
examples.trans: The bread that The baker bakes smells great.

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition a + masculine article el; al + infinitive means 'upon doing'.

examples.text: Vamos al mercado por la mañana.
examples.trans: We go to the market in the morning.

examples.text: Al abrir la puerta, sonó el timbre.
examples.trans: Upon opening the door, the bell rang.

meanings.note: Plural los panes; pan recién hecho = freshly baked bread.

examples.text: El pan es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The bread is very important here.
We talk about the bread.

meanings.note: Combines with mí/ti to form conmigo ('with me') and contigo ('with you').

examples.trans: I take coffee with hot milk.
Speak calmly, please.

meanings.note: Las siete y cuarto = seven fifteen.

examples.text: La habitación siete mira al patio.
examples.trans: Room seven overlooks the courtyard.

examples.text: Desayunamos a las siete y media.
examples.trans: We have breakfast at seven thirty.

meanings.note: Carries a written accent on í.

examples.trans: It is a wonderful piece.

examples.text: ¡Magnífica elección! ¿Quiere miel o mermelada de manzana al lado?
examples.trans: Wonderful choice! Would you like honey or apple jam on the side?

meanings.note: Plural elecciones.

examples.trans: The choice is here.

examples.text: Vemos las elecciones desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the choices from the door.

meanings.note: Sin querer = by accident; querer decir = to mean.

examples.trans: Would you like coffee or hot tea?
I opened it by accident.

meanings.note: Feminine noun: la miel.

examples.text: La miel es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The honey is very important here.
We talk about the honey.

meanings.note: Becomes u before words starting with o- or ho-.

examples.trans: Do you prefer coffee or hot tea?
Do we open today or wait until tomorrow?

meanings.note: Fruit preserve eaten at breakfast.

examples.trans: The jam is here.

examples.text: Vemos las mermeladas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the jams from the door.

meanings.note: Means both 'apple' and a square block of city buildings.

examples.trans: The apple is here.

examples.text: Vemos las manzanas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the apples from the door.

meanings.note: Al lado = on the side / next door.

examples.trans: The side is here.

examples.text: Vemos los lados desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the sides from the door.

meanings.note: Un poco de mantequilla = a little butter.

examples.text: ¿Quiere un poco de miel en el té?
examples.trans: Would you like a little honey in your tea?

examples.text: Quedan pocos minutos para el mediodía.
examples.trans: Few minutes remain until noon.

meanings.note: Spread on warm morning toast.

examples.text: La mantequilla es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The butter is very important here.
We talk about the butter.

meanings.note: Gracias por + noun/infinitive expresses 'thank you for...'.

examples.trans: Thank you very much for your help!
Thank you for coming today.

mirar.gloss: to look; to look at; to watch

meanings.en: to look; to look at; to watch
meanings.note: Needs no preposition for 'at' (mira el reloj = look at the clock).

examples.text: Mira qué sol hace esta mañana.
examples.trans: Look how sunny it is this morning.

examples.text: Miramos el mapa antes de salir.
examples.trans: We look at the map before going out.

meanings.note: After a verb, invariable tanto means 'so much' (¿por qué mira tanto?).

examples.text: ¿Cómo recuerdas eso después de tantos años?
examples.trans: How do you remember that after so many years?
Thank you for having so much patience.

su.gloss: his; her; its; their; your (polite usted/ustedes)

meanings.en: his; her; its; their; your (polite usted/ustedes)
meanings.note: Plural sus (su maleta / sus maletas).

examples.trans: Here is your key, madam.

examples.text: Sus habitaciones están en la primera planta.
examples.trans: Your rooms are on the first floor.

meanings.note: Covers wristwatches, wall clocks, and church tower clocks (plural: relojes).

examples.trans: The watch is here.

examples.text: Vemos los relojes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the watchs from the door.

meanings.note: Takes el when talking about someone (el señor Martín), no article when addressing directly (¡Buenos días, señor!).

examples.trans: The sir is here.

examples.text: Vemos los señores desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the sirs from the door.

meanings.note: Often omitted in Spanish unless adding contrast or emphasis.

examples.text: Yo abro la puerta y tú llevas la linterna.
examples.trans: I will open the door and you carry the flashlight.
It is me, please open up.

meanings.note: Expresses surprise or realization.

examples.trans: Oh, there is the blue door!

examples.text: Oh, perdona, no te había visto.
examples.trans: Oh, sorry, I had not seen you.

meanings.note: Formed from simple + -mente.

examples.trans: I simply wanted to thank you.

examples.text: Ponlo simplemente encima de la mesa.
examples.trans: Just set it on top of the table.

meanings.note: Expresses strong fondness in everyday speech.

examples.text: Adoro el olor a café recién hecho.
examples.trans: I adore the smell of freshly brewed coffee.
My grandparents adore this garden.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ending in -dad.

examples.text: La puntualidad es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The punctuality is very important here.
We talk about the punctuality.

meanings.note: Invariable cardinal number.

examples.text: La cláusula catorce protege el patio.
examples.trans: Clause fourteen protects the courtyard.

examples.text: Hay catorce sillas en el salón.
examples.trans: There are fourteen chairs in the hall.

ser.gloss: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)

meanings.en: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)
meanings.note: Used for names, professions, ownership (es mía), materials (es de madera), and clock time.

examples.text: Soy arquitecta y vivo en Valencia.
examples.trans: I am an architect and live in Valencia.
That blue suitcase is mine.

meanings.note: Warm everyday compliment in Spain (qué patio tan precioso).

examples.trans: It is a lovely piece.
Are you sure? It looks lovely and nice and warm!

meanings.note: Traditional inner courtyard at the heart of a Spanish building.

examples.trans: The courtyard is here.

examples.text: Vemos los patios desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the courtyards from the door.

meanings.note: Refers exclusively to people.

examples.text: Alguien acaba de llamar a la puerta.
examples.trans: Someone just knocked at the door.
Is anyone at the front desk?

entrar.gloss: to come in; to go in; to enter

meanings.en: to come in; to go in; to enter
meanings.note: Pairs with en in Spain (entrar en la posada).

examples.text: Entra mucha luz por el balcón.
examples.trans: Plenty of light comes in through the balcony.

examples.text: Entramos en la tienda para resguardarnos.
examples.trans: We stepped into the shop to shelter.

meanings.note: Entrar/salir corriendo = to run in / run out.

examples.text: Corro para no perder el tren.
examples.trans: I run so I do not miss the train.

examples.text: Los niños corrieron hacia la fuente.
examples.trans: The children ran toward the fountain.

meanings.note: ¡Salvados! = Saved!

examples.trans: It is a saved piece.

examples.text: Aquí están todas mis notas de la calle de esta semana. Me ha salvado.
examples.trans: All my street notes from this week are in here. You saved me.

meanings.note: Disculpe (usted) / Disculpa (tú) is polite 'excuse me'.

examples.trans: Excuse me, do you know what time it is?

examples.text: Nos disculpamos por el pequeño retraso.
examples.trans: We apologized for the brief delay.

meanings.note: Un instante = just a moment.

examples.trans: The instant is here.

examples.text: Vemos los instantes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the instants from the door.

meanings.note: Often paired with de (disfrutar de su té = enjoy your tea).

examples.text: Disfruto mucho del silencio de la mañana.
examples.trans: I really enjoy the morning quiet.
They enjoyed a peaceful dinner.

nos.gloss: us; to us; each other (¡Nos vemos!)

meanings.en: us; to us; each other (¡Nos vemos!)
meanings.note: First-person plural object/reflexive/reciprocal pronoun.

examples.trans: See you tomorrow morning!
The news makes us very glad.

meanings.note: Irregular: veo, vi, visto.

examples.text: Desde aquí veo el puente de piedra.
examples.trans: From here I see the stone bridge.
See you later in the courtyard!
